The term most bandied about is "Crony Capitalism", which really isn't capitalism at all. That's when influential businesses lobby for, and receive, special benefits from the government or from other businesses, thus restricting consumer freedom. You see it most blatantly in the media industry, such as Comcast and Time Warner convincing politicians to classify their TV service as a utility, thus allowing them a regional monopoly. A real "monopoly" as in "The only business allowed in an area", rather than the leftist "Any successful business" definition. Or most of the media industry lobbying, and getting, special treatment under various TPP/CISA/SOPE style laws. Calling this "capitalism" is a misnomer because capitalism means consumer choice and a competitive playing field. "Crony capitalism" is more similar to state-owned monopolies.

The criticism of capitalism is about the (perceived) unfair remuneration between capital and work.

The critic is about people owning a company (owning the machines, the walls, the brand) getting more money than people (engineer, worker, planner) actually building the stuff the company sells.

There are a few ways to justify why you pay stock owner and employee differently (risk taking, discrepancy between plenty of wok force and scarcity of capital). The criticism is not on the reason it should be that way but on the (perceive)d bad consequence for the society as a whole (accumulation of wealth into fewer and fewer hand, discrepancy in the political power of capital owner versus workforce) As long as capital is the driving force, wage will be naturally be set to the minimal acceptable and dividend maxed. So any form capitalism (weighting capital more than work) will be frowned upon...more or less.
